en.html:
The sword had a comfortable weight.

Not a tachi suited to warriors or mounted soldiers. This was an uchigatana for infantry alone. Less curve, shorter blade, a slightly different way of handling it—but fundamentally an easy weapon to use. No problem there.

I had thought a weapon might help my practice more than empty hands, and asked the ruler of Horigoe to lend me one.

Hikaru stood with her feet just a little apart. She raised one hand and beckoned.

An opening? The whole stance was openings. I felt I could strike from anywhere, at any time.

Not even the intimidating natural posture of a master, concealing a thousand techniques inside apparent ease. Nothing like that.

She seemed to be doing precisely one thing: standing there.

And if I still could not step in—

en.html:
Cast out that frail mind.

No self.

Leave only the will to kill.
Follow the common will of the people who did not wish Hikaru to live.

Erase every distraction. Seize the best moment.

Catch the enemy's breathing. Catch her intent. Catch her death.
Hold her fate in my hand.

Like catching the wind.
But it ought to be possible.

Reach the innermost state of no self...
And the unseen should become clear.

　無我の奥境に達すれば……
　見えざるものも<ruby>確<rt>しか</rt></ruby>と見えよう。

en.html:
—Like this.

My senses were gradually changing.
Was I approaching Kan?

The world I had known through eyes and ears became vague and uncertain. Yet my understanding grew clearer.

I grasped the garden's structure in more detail than ever before. Knew precisely where I stood.

The enemy's position, too.
In the world of Kan, Hikaru's true image emerged...

en.html:
Gone.

Hikaru had vanished from the world of Kan.

Nowhere.
...No. I could no longer perceive her.

What nonsense was this?

My Kan was immature, unsteady? No—immature or not, that was not the reason.

Right now I could sense a gardener working up a pine tree some fifty meters away. Whether that was true, I would have to check later. But movements that far away came through so vividly, and yet...

　<ruby>観<rt>カン</rt></ruby>の世界から、光が消失した。

　何処にもいない。
　……いや。認識できなくなったのだ。

　そんな馬鹿な事が。

　俺の<ruby>観<rt>カン</rt></ruby>が未熟で、定まっていないからか？
　違う――未熟の是非はともかくとして、それが原因
ではない。

　俺は今、五〇メートルばかり離れた場所で松の木に
登り仕事に勤しんでいる庭師の挙措を知覚できている。
　その真偽は後で確かめるまでわからないことだが。
そんな遠くの動きが濃密に掌握できているのに……

Plainly, obviously, Hikaru stood there.

It left him there, and laughed.
